biography:
Abdullahi Ndagi Adamu is a self-taught Nigerian visual artist from Kogi State, currently base in Abuja Nigeria. His practice explores abstraction, symbolism, memory, emotions and human experiences.

Beginning with an exploration of emotions through painting, his practice has evolved into an expressive visual language combining abstraction, symbolism, textures and figurative elements. Working primarily with acrylic and spray paint on canvas, he draws inspiration from personal experiences, everyday encounters, cultural observations and his surrounding environment.

With an academic background in Geology, his approach to art is shaped by an interest in observation, interpretation and understanding what exists beneath the visible surface.
artist_statement:
My practice is an ongoing exploration of emotions, memory, human experiences and the relationship between people and their environments.

I began painting as a way of expressing emotions, translating internal experiences into visual forms. Over time, this developed into a broader exploration of abstraction, symbolism and the different meanings that images can hold.

Working primarily with acrylic and spray paint on canvas, I combine expressive compositions, textures and symbolic elements to create works that invite observation and individual interpretation.

Influenced by my background in Geology, I am drawn to looking beyond the visible surface, exploring the layers, connections and meanings that often go unnoticed. My work draws from personal encounters, cultural observations and everyday experiences.

I am interested in how a single image can evoke different feelings and interpretations depending on what a viewer brings to it. Rather than offering fixed explanations, I approach painting as a space for questioning, remembering, discovering and connecting.
practice: Painting, Mixed Media, Acrylic, Spray Paint, Expressive Mark-Making, Abstraction, Figurative Elements
